done_when: After a full run of Forge's test suite, no process started by a test (Codex SDK stubs, app-server stubs, drivers) is left running or stopped: tests that stop a process always resume and end it in their cleanup, including when the test fails. A check at the end of the suite fails when a test left one behind and names the test.

findings.body: The supplied close run shows a new failure path: xdist worker gw5 crashed during `test_10_new_client_deploys_only_after_migration`. This guard runs only after a test yields, so it cannot check or clean up processes from a worker that dies. The unchanged deployment test starts detached containers (`tests/test_proto_deploy.py:119–120, 138`) and removes them only in its `finally` block (`tests/test_proto_deploy.py:197–205`), which also cannot run after a worker crash. Add a suite-level check and cleanup that survives worker loss and identifies the responsible test. The supplied output does not establish whether containers remained after this particular crash.
findings.title: Not done: Check and clean up processes when a test worker crashes

why: Forge's own test suite leaves stopped Codex SDK stub processes behind (63 found, up to four days old, parented to init), which pile up on developer machines
